terms.hint: Hand a task to the right person
Helping someone find their own answer
Doing right when no one's watching
Owning the outcome, good or bad

questions.q: A team member keeps missing deadlines. Best first step?
options: Do their work for them
Have a private conversation to understand why
Call them out in the team meeting
Ignore it and hope it improves
questions.explain: Lead with curiosity in private — understand the cause before you decide the fix.

options: It's vague and gentle
It's specific, timely and about behaviour
It's saved for the annual review
It's only about what went wrong
questions.explain: Specific, timely, behaviour-focused feedback is something a person can actually act on.

options: Dumping tasks you dislike
Matching the task to the person and giving context + ownership
Keeping all the important work yourself
Telling them exactly which keys to press
questions.explain: Delegate the outcome with context and authority — not just the keystrokes.

questions.q: A great way to build trust in a team is to…
options: Take credit for wins
Admit your own mistakes and follow through on commitments
Avoid all difficult conversations
Monitor everyone constantly
questions.explain: Trust grows from honesty, consistency and keeping your word.

questions.q: When should you recognise good work?
options: Only at bonus time
Specifically and soon after it happens
Never — it's their job
Only in private, never publicly
questions.explain: Timely, specific recognition reinforces exactly the behaviour you want more of.

questions.q: Coaching differs from telling because it…
options: Gives the answer faster
Helps people reach their own solution through questions
Avoids any guidance
Is only for poor performers
questions.explain: Coaching builds capability — you ask questions that help them think, not just hand over answers.
